date: 19 Mar 144[3 or 7] (head "+ Al nome di dio adi 19 di marzo 144.", last digit unclear)
title: Florentine family letter of March 1443/1447 with short runs of digit-like cipher (3, z, 8, 7, g, t) among clear news, bare
correspondents: unsigned family letter (names Benedetto, the Tornabuoni, Albertaccio, Ricciardo; Medici circle) -> "Ricciardo"? (addressee on verso not read)
language: Italian (short cipher runs in clear text)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, doc. 40 (pencil 49, old 23)
folio_note: One leaf, recto: about 20 lines of clear family news; at least four short cipher runs written in the same hand with the same dot-separated layout: line 11 end ("... tu no(n) [3 signs] z3z3z4z3"), line 13 ("g3ttz1. 93 z3z3z4z3"), line 14 ("a z3z4z3z3z#z3. 83z3. gttztt"), and a group at the end of line 18; signs are a small set of digit-like forms (3, z, 8, 7, 4) and g/t letters, repeating like a vowel-and-number cipher. Verso not opened.
status: Bare: no gloss over the runs; neighbours 39 and 41 not checked for a clear copy. Seen at 1382 px.
why: One of the oldest pieces of cipher found in the Medici archive (1440s), in a private letter; the runs are short and the sign set tiny, so the oldest-cipher question (pre-1497) is the main interest.
verify: Read the year (1443 or 1447) and the verso address at full size; transcribe the four runs; test a vowel/number substitution (the runs alternate 3 and z like vowel-consonant patterns); check docs 39 and 41.

correspondents: Tommaso Soderini (signed "Tomaso So..."), Milan -> Lorenzo de' Medici
language: Italian? (disguised text in ordinary letters; uncertain)

verify: Transcribe doc. 11 at full size and test for word substitution (cover names) versus a letter cipher in Latin letters.

title: Tommaso Soderini, Milan, August 1481: a full page of sign-and-figure cipher plus a ten-line cipher postscript, bare
correspondents: Tommaso Soderini (signed "v. Tomaso ..." on the verso), Milan -> Lorenzo de' Medici
language: Italian (sign cipher with digits; one clear date line)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza XLVIII, doc. 63 (c. 65)
folio_note: Recto: "Mag.ce v. et mag.re hon." then about 30 lines of dense continuous cipher (invented letter-like signs, Greek-like forms, digits 6, 7, 8, 9, 3, with "=" and "+" as separators; no clear word), a clear dating line, and a postscript "Dipoi scripta ..." of about 10 more cipher lines; verso: 4 cipher lines, then the signature and date.
status: Bare (1272 px): no interlinear or marginal decipherment, no filed clear text beside it (docs 62 and 64 are clear letters).
why: A long, purely enciphered despatch of 1481 from Lorenzo's ambassador in Milan, two years after the Pazzi war; about 1,500 cipher symbols, enough for a ciphertext-only attack, and the 1480s Laurentian keys (LXXII 178-188, CXIX 115-127) are the first test.
verify: Transcribe; count the sign set (homophones? "=" and "+" as word separators or nulls); test against LXXII 183 (Paolantonio Soderini, his son) and the CXIX keys; then a homophonic solver.

title: Bernardo Rucellai, Florentine orator in Milan, 1482-85: the bare pieces of his sign cipher in MAP XLVIII (seven letters and slips), with dozens of glossed siblings and four filed decipherments in the same filza
correspondents: Bernardo Rucellai (Milan) -> Lorenzo de' Medici, and via "Lionardo" (Leonardo Spina / a cover address)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza XLVIII, docs. 101, 158, 188, 189, 191, 196, 199
folio_note: 101 (c. 102r): slip, top 11 lines solid sign/figure cipher with a few clear words, then clear text; 158 (c. 161r): clear copy dated Dec 1482 with 3 cipher lines at the foot; 188 (c. 193r, endorsed 1483, "adi 14 d'aprile"): about 20 sign runs between clear words; 189 (Milan 17 Apr 1483, signed Bern.o Rucellai): runs in about 12 lines; 191 (c. 196r-v, Apr 1483): long runs in most lines and in the postscript; 196 (10 May 1483): two-line cipher postscript below the signature; 199v (17 May 1483): two-line cipher postscript beside the signature (199r is glossed).
status: Bare on these pages (contact sheet and 800 px; 188-191 at 800 px): no clear text over the runs. The same filza holds the key material: interlinear glosses on about 60 Rucellai pages (docs 97-99, 102, 105-106, 116-117, 122, 125, 128, 135, 140, 142, 153, 156, 159-161, 166, 182, 185, 190, 194-195, 198-201, 203-207, 211-213, 216-217, 219-223, 225-226, 230, 237-238, 245, 266-279, 282, 288-293) and filed decipherments: 201 c. 208 bis (of 201), 220 c. 228 (of 220 c. 229), 241 (of 239 and 240), 243 c. 254 (probably of 243 c. 253).
why: The bare Rucellai pieces can be read from the filza's own glossed letters; together with lead 2350 (LXXII 196-206, the 1482 Spina letters) they make one large Laurentian cipher corpus.
verify: Rebuild the sign table from the glossed pages and the four decipherment pairs; apply to the seven bare pieces; compare with LXXII 196-207 (lead 2350) and XLVIII 214 / 294 (see README: 294 is a cipher letter of February 1485 in the 214 sign family with its decipherment filed at c. 276).

date: 20 Aug 1486 (verso: "1486 Copia A Baccio Ugolini adi 20 d'agosto")
title: Lorenzo de' Medici to Baccio Ugolini, 20 August 1486 (copy in Lorenzo's hand, headed "Abram"): clear letter with about six code signs for persons, bare
correspondents: Lorenzo de' Medici -> Baccio Ugolini (Florentine agent, Naples/Rome)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 403 (c. 513)
folio_note: Recto headed "Abram" (a cover name?), about 30 lines in Lorenzo's hand; in the second paragraph single signs stand for persons: a box with a cross-stroke (three times), a cross, "B", a triangle, a circled cross; verso endorsed with the same box sign. MAP inventory vol. 3: "A Baccio Ugolini. (Lorenzo il Magnifico) (Firenze), (1486 mar. 17), n. 358. 1486 ago. 20, n. 403".
status: Bare (1272 px). The key sheet "Cifra col Baccio Ugolini" is in the same filza (LXXII 181: nomenclator of Re Ferrando, Duca di Calabria, Piero and Giuliano di Lorenzo ...).
why: A nomenclator-only cipher of Lorenzo himself, with the matching key in the same filza: a check of LXXII 181, not a text to solve.
verify: Match the six signs with key sheet LXXII 181; see also LXXII 358 (Lorenzo to Ugolini, 17 Mar 1486; not flagged on the sheets) and 434 ("Abraham" named twice).

date: c. 1488-89 (minute; signed on c. 509 bis "Lorenzo de Medici")
title: Lorenzo de' Medici to Giovanni Lanfredini, orator in Rome, c. 1488-89: autograph minute with about fourteen sign-cipher runs between clear words, bare
correspondents: Lorenzo de' Medici -> Giovanni Lanfredini, Florentine orator in Rome
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, doc. 504 (cc. 509-510 bis)
folio_note: c. 509r: a dense clear minute (N.S. = the pope, Virginio Orsini?) with about 8 cipher runs of 10-40 signs (÷, π, +, 2, 3, 4, Latin-letter forms) in the middle and lower half; c. 509v: about 6 more runs; c. 509 bis r: signature; c. 510 bis v: address to Lanfredini.
status: Bare (1272 px on c. 509r, 800 px on the rest): no gloss; the cipher was written into the minute by Lorenzo's chancery.
why: An outgoing cipher letter of Lorenzo il Magnifico to his key ambassador in Rome in the years of the Innocent VIII alliance; Lanfredini's incoming cipher letters (and the Laurentian key sheets) are the obvious route to the key.
verify: Transcribe the runs; test the LXXII 178-188 and CXIX 115-127 keys (none is labelled Lanfredini); look for Lanfredini's own glossed letters of 1487-89 in MAP (e.g. filze L-LX).

correspondents: Angelo Niccolini (Milan, Pavia) -> Piero di Lorenzo de' Medici
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXIV, docs. 42 (c. 90r), 49 (c. 104r), 81 (c. 177r), 90 (c. 200r)
folio_note: 42 c. 90r (Pavia 3 Aug 1492): 5-line cipher postscript; 49 c. 104r (Pavia 20 Aug 1492): one run "sul papa HH x o q m 4 d π c ÷ 11 ..."; 81 c. 177r (21 Dec 1492): one cipher line at the end; 90 c. 200r (postscript sheet, Jan 1493): one line.

why: Short, but readable from the glossed siblings; useful only as part of the Milan embassy cipher of 1492-94.

title: Piero Alamanni, Florentine orator in Milan, April 1494: two leaves with about 25 lines of mixed figure/sign cipher, bare
correspondents: Piero Alamanni (signed "Petrus Alamannus eques"), Milan -> Piero di Lorenzo de' Medici
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXIV, doc. 96 (cc. 220-221)
folio_note: c. 220r clear; c. 220v from line 6 to the foot: runs of figure/sign groups ("÷ 11 6 π b 7", "p π b v c q m", "v p y π", "22 λ p ÷ 11 o v 11 4") between clear words; c. 221r: runs in lines 1-6, 9-14, 20-24; c. 221v: first lines, signature.
status: Bare (1272 px): no interlinear clear text. The same sign family is glossed in Niccolini's and Ridolfi's letters of 1492-94 in this filza; key sheet LXXII 178 is endorsed "Alamanni Piero" (his Naples cipher of 1489-92).
why: The orator's despatch from Ludovico Sforza's court on the eve of Charles VIII's descent (spring 1494), unread, with key material in the same and the next filza.
verify: Test LXXII 178 and the table rebuilt from the glossed LXXIV letters; read c. 220v-221v.
